title: Percentages
goal: Move between fractions, decimals and percents.

quiz.prompt: A jacket costs $80 and is marked 25% off. What is the sale price?
Write the fraction 3/5 as a percentage. Give just the number.
A test has 40 questions and you answer 30 correctly. What percentage did you score?
A $200 bike is reduced by 10%, and the new price is then reduced by a further 10%. What is the final price?
quiz.explain: The first cut gives $180, and 10% of $180 is $18, leaving $162. Two 10% cuts are not the same as one 20% cut.

quiz.prompt: Three shops advertise discounts on the same price: one takes off 0.35 of it, one takes off 3/8 of it, and one takes off 30%. Which discount saves the most?
quiz.explain: 3/8 = 0.375, which beats 0.35 and 0.30. Turning each one into a decimal makes the comparison easy.

quiz.prompt: A shirt's price rises from $40 to $50. By what percentage did it increase?
quiz.explain: The rise is $10 on an original $40, and 10/40 = 0.25, which is 25%.
10% of 60 is 6 and 5% is half of that, 3, so 15% is 6 + 3 = 9.

quiz.prompt: Write the decimal 0.07 as a percentage. Give just the number.
quiz.explain: Percent means hundredths, and 0.07 is 7 hundredths, so it is 7%.

quiz.prompt: A student works out 20% of 150 by dividing 150 by 20, getting 7.5. What should they have done instead?
quiz.explain: 20% is one fifth, so you divide by 5: 150 / 5 = 30. Dividing by 20 gives 5%, not 20%.

quiz.prompt: A price goes up by 20%, and later the new price comes down by 20%. Predict how the final price compares with the original.
quiz.answer: A little below the original price
choices: A little below the original price
A little above the original price
quiz.explain: The rise is 20% of the small number and the fall is 20% of the bigger number, so $100 becomes $120 and then $96 - a 4% loss overall.

lesson_media.alt: Three-fifths, 0.60, and 60 percent are shown as equivalent parts of one whole.
lesson_media.caption: Percent means per hundred; the whole being measured still matters.

lesson_media.title: Percent means out of one hundred
lesson_media.instructions: Change the percent and the whole amount. Compare the hundred-grid, decimal and resulting part of the whole.
